- If sentiment shows strong bullish momentum (e.g., >0.4) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if followed by a spike.
- If sentiment turns bearish (e.g., < -0.3) after a price spike, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 3–7% for next 3–5 days.
- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly bullish; cap forecast at 1–2% below historical 30-day mean if sentiment < 0.2.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to mean-revert; apply a “cool-down” rule: reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days post-spike.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., +0.2, -0.5, +0.4), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment reversal point, not just historical trend.
- When sentiment is flat or negative for 3+ consecutive days, model often underestimates; add 2–5% upward bias to forecast if sentiment < 0.1 for 3+ days.
